root_cause.text: The mailbox-test driver incorrectly assumed `tx_channel` and `rx_channel` were always distinct, so in probe/remove cleanup it freed both pointers even when `rx_channel` was an alias of `tx_channel`, causing a double-free of the same mailbox channel object.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message state that “The RX channel can be aliased to the TX channel if it has a different MMIO” and “otherwise a double-free occurs,” and the patch fixes both cleanup paths by changing `if (tdev->rx_channel)` to `if (tdev->rx_channel && tdev->rx_channel != tdev->tx_channel)` before calling `mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent double-free of a shared RX/TX mailbox channel in the probe error cleanup path.
intent_record.what: The error cleanup code in mbox_test_probe() changes the second conditional free from checking only whether tdev->rx_channel is non-NULL to also requiring that tdev->rx_channel is different from tdev->tx_channel before calling mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the same mailbox channel from being freed twice during the err_free_chans cleanup path when the RX and TX channel pointers refer to the same channel, avoiding double-free behavior and associated cleanup errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid double-freeing a mailbox channel in mbox_test_remove() when RX and TX share the same channel pointer.
intent_record.what: The second conditional in mbox_test_remove() was changed from checking only whether tdev->rx_channel is non-null before calling mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel) to also requiring that tdev->rx_channel is not equal to tdev->tx_channel.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents mbox_free_channel() from being called twice on the same channel object when the receive and transmit channel pointers refer to the same channel, avoiding a double free or duplicate release during device removal.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid double-freeing a mailbox channel in mbox_test_remove() when RX and TX share the same channel pointer.

consistency_review.core_intent: Prevent double-free of a mailbox channel when RX and TX reference the same underlying channel during cleanup and remove paths.

relevance_review.reason: The changes explicitly prevent freeing the same mailbox channel twice when rx_channel aliases tx_channel in probe cleanup and remove paths, which directly matches the stated double-free root cause.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional free of rx_channel in the error cleanup path causes a double-free when rx_channel aliases tx_channel and tx_channel was already freed just above.
This unconditional free of rx_channel in remove() causes a double-free when rx_channel and tx_channel point to the same mailbox channel object and tx_channel was already freed.
The guard only checks for non-NULL rx_channel, not whether it is distinct from tx_channel, allowing the subsequent free to run on an already-freed aliased pointer.
This condition assumes rx_channel is independently owned whenever non-NULL, failing to account for aliasing with tx_channel and enabling the later double-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional free releases rx_channel even when it aliases tdev->tx_channel, which may already have been freed just before, directly causing the double-free in both probe error cleanup and remove paths.
This guard only checks whether rx_channel is non-NULL and incorrectly treats it as independently owned, failing to ensure it is distinct from tx_channel before the subsequent free.

Author: Wolfram Sang <wsa+renesas@sang-engineering.com>
Date:   Fri Apr 10 14:53:00 2026 +0200

    mailbox: mailbox-test: free channels on probe error
    
    On probe error, free the previously obtained channels. This not only
    prevents a leak, but also UAF scenarios because the client structure

    Link: https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260327151217.5327-2-wsa%2Brenesas
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the exact cleanup logic added on the probe error path, which is enough to assess the root cause. In the new `err_free_chans:` block, the function unconditionally frees both channel pointers independently: `if (tdev->tx_channel) mbox_free_channel(tdev->tx_channel);` and `if (tdev->rx_channel) mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel);`. Per the stated root cause, `rx_channel` may alias `tx_channel` rather than being distinct. This code does not check whether `tdev->rx_channel == tdev->tx_channel` before freeing both, so if they are the same object it will free the same mailbox channel twice. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. The fix would require handling the alias case and avoiding a second free when both pointers reference the same channel, but no such check exists here.

di
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the relevant allocation/request paths in probe and the cleanup path in remove. The root cause is freeing both channel pointers even when they may alias the same mailbox channel object. In this commit, `mbox_test_probe()` independently assigns both pointers: `tdev->tx_channel = mbox_test_request_channel(pdev, "tx");` and `tdev->rx_channel = mbox_test_request_channel(pdev, "rx");` with no check that they are distinct. Then `mbox_test_remove()` unconditionally frees each non-NULL pointer separately: `if (tdev->tx_channel) mbox_free_channel(tdev->tx_channel);` and `if (tdev->rx_channel) mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel);`. If `rx_channel` is an alias of `tx_channel`, both conditionals execute and the same channel object is freed twice. There is no protective logic such as comparing the pointers before the second free, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present.
